questions.question: Discuss the role of sulphonylureas in controlling diabetes. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of sulphonylureas in controlling diabetes.
  • • Increase body's production of insulin – ¼ mark
  • • May provoke hypoglycemia and their use requires regular timing of meals and snacks
  • - ¼ mark
  • • Tolbutamide is the safest of sulphonylureas. Effective action is 6 to 8 hrs and should
  • be taken 2 to 3 times a day - ¼ mark
  • • Chloropropamide can be given as single dose of 100 to 375 mg/day. Toxic effect such
  • as jaundice, drug rashes and blood dyscrasia (abnormal cells of blood) is seen in long
  • term use. - ¼ mark

questions.question: Differentiate elemental diet and semi elemental diet / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate elemental diet and semi elemental diet
  • Elemental diet – also known as hydrolysed formulas.
  • • Recommended for patients with limited gastrointestinal function.
  • • Normal foods replaced by preparation of protein or amino acids, fats and
  • carbohydrates in easily assimilable form
  • • More expensive than general purpose formula – 2. 5 marks
  • Semi elemental diet – they are peptide based formulas also contain free amino acids.
  • • Carhohydrates are usually hydrolysed.
  • • Fat content is low – some may contain MCT or SFA.
  • • Beneficial for patients with short bowel syndrome or limited GI function – 2.5
  • marks

questions.question: Explain the nutritional requirements in influenza / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the nutritional requirements in influenza
  • Influenza – Short duration fever. Spreads from person to person by inhalation of
  • virus- 1 mark
  • Nutritional requirements (4 marks for Nutritional requirements)
  • Energy – 50% increase in calorie requirement due to increased temperature and tissue
  • destruction
  • Protein – About 100gm is recommended
  • Carbohydrate – high CHO to replenish glycogen storage
  • Fat – Moderate fat – avoid fried foods
  • Minerals – Sufficient intake of sodium chloride to compensate electrolyte loss
  • Vitamins – Increased requirement of Vitamin A, C and B complex vitamins.
  • Fluid – liberal. 2.5 – 5 lit/day is recommended.

questions.question: Explain bolus method of infusion and continuous method of infusion in enteral feeding / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain bolus method of infusion and continuous method of infusion in enteral
  • feeding
  • Bolus infusion - When patient is clinically stable, syringe bolus method is
  • recommended.
  • • They are less expensive than pump or gravity feeding method.
  • • 60 ml syringe is used to infuse the formula.
  • • If bloating occurs weight for 10- 15 minutes.
  • • Usually the patient can tolerate 500ml at each feeding – 2.5 marks
  • Continuous infusion – appropriate for patients who do not tolerate large volume
  • infusions.
  • • Recommended for patients with compromised gastrointestinal function.
  • • Feeding provided usually 18- 24 hours daily.
  • • Formulas with 300- 500mOsm/kg can be started at full strength.- 2.5 marks

questions.question: Explain the complications and monitoring in parenteral nutrition / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the complications and monitoring in parenteral nutrition
  • Complications-
  • Catheter related complications – cardiac arrhythmia, air embolus, thrombosis,
  • perforation and sepsis- 2.5 marks
  • Metabolic complications – hyperglycemia, osmotic diuresis, azotemia, electrolye
  • disturbance, acid base change, fatty degeneration of liver. – 2.5 marks
  • Nutritional complications – loss of lean body weight, bone demineralization,
  • vitamin deficiency and toxicity essential fatty acid deficiency, trace metal deficiency
  • – 2.5 marks
  • Monitoring- routine monitoring is essential to avoid the risk of complications.
  • Monitor the signs of infection, chills, fever and tachycardia, sudden hyperglycemia
  • and elevated WBC. – 2.5 marks

questions.question: Explain AIDS - pathology, transmission and clinical manifestation / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain AIDS – pathology, transmission and clinical manifestations
  • Pathology – HIV invades the genetic core of CD+ or T helper lymphocyte cells leads
  • to its depletion and results in immunodeficiency- 1 mark
  • Transmission – transmitted by body fluids. 3 marks
  • Prenatal transmission - 2marks
  • Clinical manifestation
  • Acute HIV – it is 4-7 weeks immediately after primary infection. Fever, malaise,
  • lymphadenopathy syndrome, pharyngitis, headache, myalgia may occur.- 1 mark
  • Asymptomatic HIV – Last for 10 years. Decrease in lean body mass, vitamin B12
  • deficiency. -1 mark
  • Symptomatic HIV – fever, sweat, skin problems and fartigue. Decline in nutrient
  • status and body composition – 1 mark
  • AIDS – last stage of HIV. A small proportion infected with HIV may die. – 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the principles of diet and dietary management in diabetes. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the principles of diet and dietary management in diabetes
  • • Principles of diet – Low calorie, low carbohydrate, adequate protein, low fat,
  • high fibre diet - 1 mark
  • • Energy – 25 kcal/kg body weight - ½ mark
  • • Carbohydrate – 45-60 per cent of total calorie – include polysaccharides like
  • whole grains – high fibre low GI foods preferred – low CHO improve insulin
  • sensitivity – 2 marks
  • • Protein – 15 – 20 % of calorie – supply essential amino acids for tissue repair –
  • promotes satiety – 0.8 – 1g/kg body weight can be given – in type 1, 1-1.5 g/kg
  • body weight – 0.6 g/kg body weight in renal condition – 2 marks
  • • Fat – visible fat 20 – 25 g/day – saturated fat <7 % total calories – 15 – 25 %
  • total calories, high in PUFA – include omega 3 fatty acids - 1 mark
  • • Dietary fibre – lower insulin requirement – increase tissue insulin sensitivity –
  • decrease serum cholesterol and triglyceride values – aid in weight control and
  • lower BP – soluble and insoluble fibre – 2 marks
  • • Vitamins – supply antioxidant vitamin E and C – vitamin B12 – ½ mark
  • • Minerals – chromium – zinc – sodium and potassium – 1 mark
